source_review: Both kernels derive Suspend from actual TaskYield bodies and direct call closure. Ordinary Call, FunctionRef, ForeignFunctionRef and scoped thread roots reject those targets. No producer effect flag grants authority.

Worker whitelist admits only the actually lowered scalar storage/arithmetic/CFG profile; it excludes calls, address/environment/owned values, foreign operations, callbacks and wakers. Fast close is justified only by that independently checked absence of external users.

Actual owner-head loans and ancestry reject competing activation and live-borrow destruction. Nullable allocation failure is a defined empty state. Ready is delivered once; early finish_destroy traps before freeing; default Drop cancels/closes before free.

Native lowering persists actual values across branch/backedge/yield continuations. One request meter shares the remaining Copy/LargeCopy planning balance, including parallel batches. Unused yielding workers receive runtime allocation imports.
The NoInline init boundary preserves explicit fallibility at O2. The same source observes AVF on success and AN/exit10 under allocator failure; no unmeasured zero-cost assertion is made.

limitations: Public semantic TaskInterface/exported physical SABI, general owned spills/defer, returned retained registration, external callback/waker drain and late wake remain unestablished.
General Mutex<T>/owned constructors and full Transfer/Share are separate obligations. Native Windows and Rust runtime/RSS/compile/maintenance comparisons were not run.
